senses: A theatre or theater, playhouse; stage.
la:noun:theatrum.html:
thĕātrum, i, n., = θέατρον,
a playhouse, theatre (cf.: scena, spectaculum, ludus).
Lit.: num theatrum, gymnasia, porticus, etc. ... rem publicam efficiebat?: theatrum ut commune sit,: castra munita ... alterā (ex parte) a theatro, quod est ante oppidum,; : populi sensus maxime theatro et spectaculis perspectus est,: aliquid totius theatri clamore dicere,: consessus theatri,: in vacuo laetus sessor plausorque theatro,; : hos arto stipata theatro Spectat Roma potens,: Philippus in acie tutior quam in theatro fuit,; cf. sqq.; ; ; : exeamus e theatro,i. e. cease to speak of actors,.—Of the Greek theatre, which served as a place for public meetings, ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
In gen., any open space for exhibiting martialgames, ; .—
Like our theatre, for the spectators assembled in a theatre, a theatrical audience: frequentissimum,: consensus theatri,: tunc est commovendum theatrum, cum ventum est ad ipsum illud Plaudite,.—Plur.: qui (modi) totis theatris maestitiam inferunt,; : tota saepe theatra exclamasse barbare,; cf.: spissa theatra,.—
Trop., a place of exhibition, theatre, stage, for any public act: nullum theatrum virtuti conscientia majus est,: magno theatro (ea familiaritas) spectata est,openly, publicly,; cf.: quasi in aliquo terrarum orbis theatro versari,; : in theatro terrarum orbis esse,: optimus quisque praeceptor frequentiā gaudet ac majore se theatro dignum putat,.

la:noun:thesaurus.html:
thēsaurus (old form thensaurus, prol. p. ciii. Ritschl; cf. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 590; collat. form thensau-rum, n., ), i, m., = θησαυρός.
Any thing laid or stored up, a hoard, treasure, provision, store.
Lit.: TABVLARIVS THENSAVRORVM,: thensaurum effodere,; ; ; : thesaurum defodere ... invenire,: nec vero quemquam senem audivi oblitum, quo loco thesaurum obruisset,: non exercitus neque thensauri praesidia regni sunt, verum amici,: intactis opulentior Thesauris Arabum,.—
Law t. t., treasure trove: thensaurus est vetus quaedam depositio pecuniae, cujus non exstat memoria, ut jam dominum non habeat,; ; Cod. 10, 15, 1.—
Trop. (very rare): thesaurus mali,a great quantity,: stupri, id. Fragm. ap. ; cf.: augent ex pauxillo; thensaurum inde pariunt,: thesauros penitus abditae fraudis vultu laeto tegentes,. —
Of persons, a treasure, loved one, a valued or dear object: Di. Quid, amator novos quispiam? Ast. Integrum et plenum adortust thensaurum, ; cf. : eccum lenonem, incedit, thensaurum meum,; cf.: thensaurus copiarum,.—
A place where any thing is stored up, a storehouse, treasure - chamber, treasure - vault, treasury (cf.: cella, armarium).
Lit.: monedula condens semina in thesauros cavernarum,; cf. poet., of the cells of bees, : admonent quidam, esse thesaurum publicum sub terrā saxo quadrato septum,: Proserpinae,; ; ; cf. poet. of the Lower World: postquam est Orcino traditus thesauro, Naev. ap. .—
Esp., a strong-box, treasure-chest: cum thesaurum effregisset heres,: apertis thesauris suis,.—
Trop., a repository, conservatory, magazine, collection, : quid dicam de thesauro rerum omnium, memoria?; ; cf.: thesauri argumentorum,: suppeditat nobis Atticus noster de thesauris suis quos et quantos viros,: thesauros oportet esse non libros, Plin. praef. § 17; cf.: mihi quoties aliquid abditum quaero, ille thesaurus est,a literary storehouse,.—
The title of a Greek play by Philemon, upon which Plautus founded the Trinummus, .
